findings.title: Docstring falsely claims the token is a JWT
findings.why: The docstring reads "Returns a signed JWT valid for 24 hours." The return value is `hashlib.sha1(...).hexdigest() + "." + str(user_id)` — a plain SHA-1 hex digest concatenated with the user ID, separated by a dot. This is not a JWT (which would be three base64url-encoded segments). Callers relying on JWT-parsing libraries will fail, and security reviewers auditing "JWT usage" will be misled.
findings.fix:
"""Returns a token of the form ``<sha1hex>.<user_id>``.

The SHA-1 digest is computed over ``user_id|timestamp|JWT_SECRET``.
Note: the token format is NOT a JWT and is NOT verified on the read
path — ``current_user_id()`` extracts the user ID from the suffix
without validating the digest or checking the embedded timestamp.
"""

findings.title: Docstring falsely claims tokens expire after 24 hours
findings.why: The docstring states "valid for 24 hours" but `current_user_id()` — the only consumer — does not parse the token, verify the digest, or inspect the embedded timestamp. A token issued by `issue_token` is valid forever. The claim of 24-hour expiry is factually false and creates a false sense of security.
findings.fix: Add to the docstring: "There is no expiry enforcement — ``current_user_id()`` does not validate the digest or the timestamp embedded in the token."

findings.title: Security-critical function has no docstring
findings.why: `current_user_id` is the sole authentication gate for `search`, `create_note`, and `filter_notes`. It has no docstring. The function accepts any string matching `<anything>.<integer>` as a valid identity — the SHA-1 prefix is never verified. This behaviour (and its security implication) is entirely invisible to callers.
findings.fix:
"""Extract the user ID from an auth token.

Args:
    token: A string of the form ``<sha1hex>.<user_id>`` as produced by
           ``issue_token()``, or any value accepted by the
           ``Authorization`` header.

Returns:
    The integer user ID parsed from the suffix of ``token``, or
    ``None`` if ``token`` is falsy or not in the expected two-part
    format.

Warning:
    The SHA-1 prefix is **not** verified. Any string of the form
    ``<anything>.<integer>`` is accepted as a valid identity.
    Tokens do not expire.
"""

findings.title: Security-critical function has no docstring
findings.why: `isAdmin` controls access to the admin deletion endpoint. It has no docstring. The bare string comparison against a hardcoded config value (`ADMIN_BYPASS_TOKEN = "letmein-admin"`) is invisible to callers, as is the fact that admin access is controlled solely by a single static secret with no per-user identity.
findings.fix:
"""Return True if the request carries a valid admin token.

Checks the ``X-Admin-Token`` header against the ``ADMIN_BYPASS_TOKEN``
configuration value using a plain string equality comparison (not a
constant-time comparison). Returns ``False`` for any other value,
including an absent header.

Args:
    request_headers: A Werkzeug/Flask Headers object (or any
        mapping) providing a ``get`` method.

Returns:
    bool
"""

findings.title: eval-based function has no docstring — critical undisclosed risk
findings.why: `applyFilterExpression` passes the caller-supplied `expression` string directly to `eval()` inside a list comprehension with no sandboxing, no allowlist, and no validation. This is a remote code execution vector. The function has no docstring at all, so the eval usage and its security implications are completely invisible. The PR description describes this as "simple Python-ish predicates so power users can write whatever they want" — which confirms the intent to accept arbitrary Python, making the missing documentation even more critical.
findings.evidence:
def applyFilterExpression(notes, expression):
    return [n for n in notes if eval(expression)]
findings.fix:
"""Filter ``notes`` by evaluating ``expression`` against each note.

Args:
    notes: Iterable of note rows as returned by ``search_notes``.
    expression: A Python expression string evaluated with ``eval()``
        for each note ``n`` in the list. The variable ``n`` is
        available inside the expression.

Returns:
    A list of notes for which ``expression`` evaluated to a truthy
    value.

WARNING:
    This function calls ``eval()`` on unsanitised, caller-supplied
    input with no sandboxing. It is a remote code execution
    vulnerability — any Python expression, including os.system()
    calls or file reads, will be executed in the server process.
    Do NOT expose this to untrusted input.
"""

findings.title: Public DB function has no docstring; silent exception swallowing undocumented
findings.why: `delete_note` has no docstring. Its bare `except: pass` block silently discards all exceptions — callers (including `remove_note`) have no way to determine whether the delete succeeded or failed. This is not documented anywhere, making it impossible for callers to implement error handling.
findings.fix:
"""Delete the note with the given ID from the database.

Args:
    note_id: The integer primary key of the note to delete.

Returns:
    None

Note:
    All database exceptions are silently swallowed. The function
    returns ``None`` regardless of whether the delete succeeded,
    the row did not exist, or an error occurred. Callers cannot
    detect failure.
"""

findings.title: DELETE route has no docstring; auth requirement and silent-failure behaviour invisible
findings.why: `remove_note` has no docstring. Two important behaviours are invisible: (1) the route requires a valid `X-Admin-Token` header and returns 403 otherwise; (2) it calls `delete_note` which silently swallows exceptions, so a 204 response does not guarantee the note was actually deleted.
findings.fix:
"""DELETE /notes/<note_id> — remove a note by ID (admin only).

Requires the ``X-Admin-Token`` header to match the configured
``ADMIN_BYPASS_TOKEN`` value. Returns 403 if the header is absent
or incorrect.

Returns 204 on apparent success. Note that the underlying
``delete_note()`` silently swallows database errors, so a 204
response does not guarantee the row was actually deleted.
"""

findings.title: POST filter route has no docstring; eval risk and traceback leak invisible
findings.why: `filter_notes` has no docstring. Two significant behaviours are invisible: (1) it delegates to `applyFilterExpression` which calls `eval()` on the caller-supplied `expression` field — a remote code execution risk; (2) on any exception it returns the full server-side traceback in the JSON response body (`"trace": traceback.format_exc()`), leaking internal paths, module names, and stack frames to callers.
findings.fix:
"""POST /notes/filter — filter the authenticated user's notes.

Request body (JSON):
    expression (str): A Python expression evaluated against each note
        row ``n`` via ``eval()``. Any valid Python is accepted —
        this is a remote code execution risk and must not be exposed
        to untrusted callers.

Returns:
    200 with a JSON array of matching note rows on success.
    500 with ``{"error": "...", "trace": "<full traceback>"}`` on
        any exception — the full server traceback is included in the
        error response, leaking internal implementation details.
"""

not_checked: sample-project/config.py (no new symbols, only a new constant ADMIN_BYPASS_TOKEN with no docstring convention in that file)
